# Federation Principles v0.1

**Status:** Draft (FC-0.1) · **Scope:** All sovereign domains · **Evidence:** FFR-1, FGI-R1, BFR-1, `federation/README.md`

---

## P1 — Contracts, not canon

The federation owns **versioned interchange contracts** and **reference registries**. It does not own domain data, graphs, scores, narratives, or stewardship decisions.

## P2 — Sovereignty is non-negotiable

Every interchange record carries `sovereign_id`. No silent cross-sovereign write. No merged truth store.

## P3 — Observation before interpretation

Federation may standardize **what was observed** (pinned, checksum-sealed). Federation must not standardize **what it means** for a domain.

## P4 — Replay stays sovereign

Replay execution, rules versions, and validation outcomes remain in the domain that owns the observation. Federation may reference attestations; it does not re-run domain pipelines.

## P5 — Ambiguity is explicit

Unknown, conflicted, and observer-relative states must remain visible. Federation contracts forbid collapsing uncertainty into false certainty.

## P6 — Standards require evidence

A contract becomes a **Federation Standard** only after schema publication, registry alignment, and **at least two sovereign normative fixtures** (T3 conformance) — unless a single-sovereign pilot is explicitly labeled non-standard.

## P7 — Reference is not authority

Hosting schemas, reviews, or a reference OAT implementation does not make any repository the federation platform (FFR-1, FGI-R1, `FEDERATION.md`).

## P8 — Anti-centralization by default

When in doubt, preserve domain autonomy. Federation growth must not become ontology imperialism, replay imperialism, or interpretation capture.

## P9 — Continuity without coercion

Federation exists to make **longitudinal continuity reconstructable across boundaries** — not to prescribe recovery, behavior, or canonical flourishing.

## P10 — Ethics follow transparency

Emergence, validation, and trace capabilities are **visibility layers** — not hidden optimization, agency simulation, or covert governance (FGI-R1 emergence safety; BFR-1 EG exclusions).
